title: Almost dense finite locally free locus for a finite groupoid
statement: Let $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ be a groupoid scheme [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. Assume $s,t$ are finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. For a morphism $a:T\to U$, the restricted groupoid has object scheme $T$ and arrow scheme $T\times_{a,U,s}R\times_{t,U,a}T$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with induced source, target and groupoid operations. Then there are an open subscheme $W\subseteq U$ and a closed subscheme $W'\subseteq W$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion] such that both are $R$-invariant (their inverse images under $s$ and $t$ agree as subschemes of $R$), $W'\hookrightarrow W$ induces a homeomorphism on underlying spaces, $U=t(s^{-1}(\overline{|W|}))$ as sets, and the source and target of the restricted groupoid on $W'$ are finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free].

proof.text: Choose the invariant closed filtration $Z_n$ of [lem-sfb-finite-groupoid-invariant-rank-filtration], and put $D_r=Z_{r-1}\setminus Z_r$. Its intersection is empty, and the source over $D_r$ is finite locally free of degree $r$. We construct pairwise disjoint invariant opens $W_r\subseteq U$ and invariant closed subschemes $W'_r\subseteq W_r$ with $|W'_r|=|W_r|$, maintaining $U\setminus|Z_n|\subseteq C_n:=\bigcup_{1\leq r\leq n}\sigma(\overline{|W_r|})$, where $\sigma(A)=t(s^{-1}(A))$. For $n=0$ take $C_0=\varnothing$; the asserted inclusion holds because $Z_0=U$.

source.place: Tag 0ABA (lemma-finite-flat-over-almost-dense-subscheme), first paragraph and induction hypotheses

proof.text: For any already constructed $W_r$, its saturation $F_r=\sigma(\overline{|W_r|})$ is invariant by [lem-sfb-groupoid-subset-saturation-invariant]. It is closed: $s^{-1}(\overline{|W_r|})$ is closed by continuity of $s$, and $t$ sends closed subsets to closed subsets by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres], since $t$ is finite. Thus each finite union $C_n=\bigcup_{r\leq n}F_r$ is closed and invariant, with $s^{-1}(C_n)=t^{-1}(C_n)$.

Given the construction through $n$, set $W_{n+1}=U\setminus(|Z_{n+1}|\cup C_n)$ with its open subscheme structure. Since $U\setminus|Z_n|\subseteq C_n$, this open lies in $|Z_n|\setminus|Z_{n+1}|$. Its underlying set is therefore exactly the set prescribed in the source, $|Z_n|\setminus(|Z_{n+1}|\cup C_n)$. Complements and unions preserve the equality of inverse images defining set invariance; hence $W_{n+1}$ is invariant as an open subscheme. Each earlier $W_r$ lies in $F_r$ by the identity section, so is disjoint from $W_{n+1}$.

source.place: Tag 0ABA (lemma-finite-flat-over-almost-dense-subscheme), inductive construction of the next open; corrected indexing in the openness argument

proof.text: Define $W'_{n+1}=Z_n\times_U W_{n+1}$. On an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $W_{n+1}$ this is $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ for the restricted ideal of $Z_n$, so it is closed; its support is all of $W_{n+1}$ by step 3. Pullback intersections of the two equal subschemes $s^{-1}(Z_n)=t^{-1}(Z_n)$ and $s^{-1}(W_{n+1})=t^{-1}(W_{n+1})$ show scheme-theoretic invariance of $W'_{n+1}$. It is an open subscheme of $D_{n+1}$. Thus its source is the open restriction of the degree-$(n+1)$ map in [lem-sfb-finite-groupoid-invariant-rank-filtration]. Finiteness persists by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a); flatness and local finite presentation persist because the same local rings and local affine presentations compute them on an open restriction. Its fibres are the same fibres, so the degree stays $n+1$. Inversion is an involutive isomorphism interchanging source and target, hence the target has the same properties.

source.place: Tag 0ABA (lemma-finite-flat-over-almost-dense-subscheme), inductive construction of the thickening and rank assertion

proof.text: Extend $C_n$ by $F_{n+1}=\sigma(\overline{|W_{n+1}|})$. A point outside $Z_{n+1}$ either lies in $C_n$ or, by step 3, belongs to $W_{n+1}$, which is contained in $F_{n+1}$ by the identity section. This proves $U\setminus|Z_{n+1}|\subseteq C_{n+1}$ and closes the induction. In particular its initial stage is $W_1=W'_1=U\setminus Z_1$; no rank-zero piece is needed.

source.place: Tag 0ABA (lemma-finite-flat-over-almost-dense-subscheme), verification of induction property (3), including the initial stage

proof.text: Let $W=\bigcup_{r\geq1}W_r$ with its open subscheme structure. The pairwise disjoint open cover identifies $W$ with $\coprod_r W_r$. Glue $W'_r\hookrightarrow W_r$ to $W'\hookrightarrow W$: on each member use its defining ideal, and on the empty intersections compatibility is unique. The resulting quotient structure sheaves define a closed immersion by its affine-local description. Since each $|W'_r|=|W_r|$, this closed immersion is a homeomorphism on underlying spaces. Invariance of $W$ is equality of the unions of its inverse images. For $W'$ the two pullbacks agree on each common open inverse image of $W_r$, where they are the equal pullbacks of $W'_r$; hence they agree globally.

source.place: Tag 0ABA (lemma-finite-flat-over-almost-dense-subscheme), disjoint unions of the open pieces and their closed thickenings

proof.text: For an invariant monomorphism $W'\to U$, the double restriction $W'\times_{U,s}R\times_{t,U}W'$ identifies with either single inverse image: the equality of the two inverse-image subschemes makes the second condition automatic, and a monomorphism has unique lifts. Consequently the restricted source is a base change of the finite map $s$, and is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a). Above each open-and-closed piece $W'_r$ it is exactly the source constructed in step 4, so it is flat at every point. Every point also has the local affine finite presentation furnished on that piece, hence the global source is locally of finite presentation. By the definition it is finite locally free. Inversion identifies the restricted target with the restricted source, so the target is finite locally free as well.

source.place: Tag 0ABA (lemma-finite-flat-over-almost-dense-subscheme), final finite locally free conclusion, with finiteness obtained by a single global base change

proof.text: For any $u\in|U|$, the empty intersection $\bigcap_n|Z_n|$ gives some $n$ with $u\notin|Z_n|$. By the induction $u\in C_n$, hence $u\in\sigma(\overline{|W_r|})$ for some $r\leq n$. Since $W_r\subseteq W$, monotonicity of closure, inverse image and image gives $u\in\sigma(\overline{|W|})$. This proves $|U|=t(s^{-1}(\overline{|W|}))$. Together with steps 6 and 7 it gives all four required clauses.

source.place: Tag 0ABA (lemma-finite-flat-over-almost-dense-subscheme), last paragraph: use of the empty intersection

It is not a duplicate of lem-a1-affine-groupoid-invariant-rank-strata, which assumes affine and already finite locally free. (5) Steps 1-8 are correct. The induction U∖Z_n ⊆ C_n is stated with its base case. C_n is closed because t is finite and therefore a closed map. The worker says the Stacks openness sentence cites the wrong index; I checked line 2509 and they are right, and their formula W_{n+1}=U∖(Z_{n+1}∪C_n) fixes it. W'_{n+1}=Z_n×_U W_{n+1} is an open subscheme of D_{n+1}. Gluing along the disjoint open cover is done per piece. Global finiteness comes from base change of s once the invariant monomorphism collapses the double restriction; flatness and finite presentation are checked per piece. (6) Edge cases checked: U empty, the trivial groupoid, a constant finite group, infinitely many ranks on a non-quasi-compact U, and non-reduced U.
